name: aurora_lifecycle
//: §11a's display lifecycle and the cross-fade, both of which are TEMPORAL and neither of which
a still can show. Two clips at two completely different time bases, which is the whole point:
aurora_lifecycle_glide   TickLapse, 10 ticks/frame — 20 in-game minutes with the sun, the
weather and the shadows held still. This is the ONLY instrument that
can show the stepping fix. The bug was the field advancing once per
32-tick refresh sweep instead of once per tick, and an hour-based
Timelapse steps 2500 ticks a frame — 78 sweeps — so it cannot
distinguish the two behaviours at all.
aurora_lifecycle_night   Timelapse, 0.25 h/frame across a whole night — displays spawning,
drifting, fading and being replaced elsewhere, plus the clear sky
the bands guarantee between concurrent ones. This is the opposite
framing and needs it: one display lives 2.5-4.2 in-game hours, which
at 10 ticks a frame would be 60,000 frames.
aurora_lifecycle_bakein is a deliberate throwaway that is still worth keeping: it films the
field filling itself in from zero over the first ~32 tick-changes. §11a ships no priming pass on
purpose (a full bake is a dropped frame at exactly the moment a player looks up) and relies on an
unbaked row being RGBA(0,0,0,0), i.e. invisible under additive blending. This is that claim on
film, and it also guarantees the glide clip that follows starts from a fully formed field rather
than filming the fill-in and calling it motion.
Latitude 20 / day 40 / hour 21 is deep night well clear of both twilights, so NightVisibility
sits at 1 and the curtain runs at its full 0.55 rather than somewhere on the ramp. The night
sweep then runs forward through 05:00, crossing midnight, which AdvanceTime rolls over correctly
where a sequence of absolute SetTimes would rewind a day mid-clip.
Shot on the SHIPPED preset, not Realistic. The aurora is additive and Cinematic's brighter night
floor is the harder background to read against, so this is the honest view rather than the
flattering one — the opposite of the night-floor scenarios, which need Realistic because a floor
cannot be seen through an accessibility clamp at all.
RUN STANDALONE. It starts a GameCondition, and the harness only reloads between suite scenarios
for MAP residue, so a live Aurora leaks into whatever runs next.
Pinned rather than assumed. run_test.sh does not reset PERSISTED mod settings between runs,
and realistic_preset writes straight through to them, so a preceding night-floor scenario can
leave Realistic latched and this clip would be shot against a black night nobody ships.
Setting it false re-applies Cinematic, which is the shipped default — the harder and honest
background for an additive effect.

steps.//: Peak: past the condition's hour-long fade-in, deep night, curtain enabled.
And §11's flat wash stepped back to vanilla's peak because the curtain is carrying it.
A still of the fully formed field, for an inline A/B against the pre-change build.

//: fromHour IS PINNED EXPLICITLY, and must be. Timelapse always desugars its first frame to a
SetTime, including in the steps/stepHours form, where fromHour simply defaults to 0 — which
here would rewind the clock from ~21:38 back to midnight of the SAME day. SetTime is
absolute and pins the day, so that is a ~21-hour rewind: the Aurora condition un-ages back
through its own fade-in, and the display schedule's age goes negative and clamps, restarting
the sequence at slot 0. The clip would open on a display that had already been on screen.
22 is just ahead of where the two tick lapses leave the clock (21:00 + 1600 ticks), so the
pin is a ~15-minute step FORWARD rather than a jump back. 22 -> 5 wraps past midnight, which
AdvanceTime rolls over correctly; seven in-game hours is two to three generations of the
shorter slots, so displays are seen being replaced rather than merely fading.
